text:
The merit of parents

Among the signs of the merit of parents is that Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the terrors of the Day of Judgment in His saying:
يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ ۚ يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ (11) وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَأَخِيهِ (12) وَفَصِيلَتِهِ الَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ (13) وَمَن فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ

And in another place He said:
يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ (34) وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ (35) وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ

So He mentioned that a person flees from his parents, but did not mention them among those he would sacrifice, because of their standing. And Allah knows best.

قَالَ فَمَنْ رَبُّكُمَا يَا مُوسَى
He addressed the two of them (Aaron and Moses) but directed the call to just one, Moses.
This can carry two meanings:
The first is that Moses is the root of the prophethood, and Aaron is his deputy and follower.
The second is that Pharaoh used his cunning and called on Moses to do the talking, because he knew Aaron was the more eloquent of the two. It is said that Moses had a difficulty in his tongue, which is why Moses said to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic: "وَأَخِي هَارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِيَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِي"
And Pharaoh's words point to this meaning: "أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِّنْ هَٰذَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ" that is, I am better than this man who cannot speak clearly. And Allah knows best.

قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَا إِلَى الصَّخْرَةِ فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الْحُوتَ وَمَا أَنسَانِيهُ إِلَّا الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ ۚ وَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ عَجَبًا
As for the word "عجبا" (amazingly), one reading is to pause after it, which makes it the words of Moses' young companion, as if he said, "How amazing was its way into the sea!" The reason for the amazement, it is said, is that the fish had been roasted and partly eaten.
The other reading is to pause before it, so that "وَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ" is one sentence, then a stop, and then the words "عَجَبًا" as if Moses' young companion said the first sentence, and our master Moses was struck with wonder and said "How amazing!" And Allah knows best.

In my humble opinion, the most frightening verse in the Quran is: "قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِالْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالًا (103) الَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا"
Imagine your whole life going to waste, while you were fully convinced that you were doing the right thing.

It is reported that Iblis came to Jesus (peace be upon him) and said to him: "Don't you claim that nothing will befall you except what Allah has written for you?" He said: "Yes." Iblis said: "Then throw yourself down from this mountain, for if safety is decreed for you, you will be safe." Jesus said: "Accursed one! Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, tests His servants; it is not for a servant to test his Lord."

The happiest and the most miserable thing a person can go through is to dream. The happiness is in reaching what you may never be able to reach in reality, and the misery is in knowing for certain that you will never get there.

The deed is done, you who were nothing yesterday, you whose limbs will scatter into nothing tomorrow. With what face will you meet your Lord? Is what you gain from desire worth even a word of reproach?!

Habits are another religion
I have seen that people's habits have overcome their living by the Shariah. They feel uneasy about doing a thing only because the habit isn't there, not because the Shariah forbids it!

The commentators mention that when the Prophet (peace be upon him) conquered Makkah, Uthman ibn Talha ibn Abd al-Dar hurried to lock the door of the Kaaba (he was the keeper who held its key), climbed onto its roof, and refused to hand the key to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). He said to them: "If I knew he was the Messenger of Allah, I would not have withheld the key from him."

So Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) got up, twisted his arm, and took the key from him by force. He opened the House, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) went in, prayed two units of prayer inside the Kaaba, and came out.

Then his uncle al-Abbas asked him to give him the key, so that he would hold both the providing of water to the pilgrims and the keeping of the Kaaba. Then the words of the Almighty came down: "إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا بِالْعَدْلِ"

So the Prophet (peace be upon him) ordered that the key be returned to Uthman ibn Talha and that an apology be made to him. When Ali went to him, Uthman said: "You hurt me and forced me, and now you come being gentle."

Ali said: "Allah has revealed a Quranic verse about you," and then recited the verse to him.

Uthman said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the Messenger of Allah."

صغيرٌ يطلبُ الكِبرا .. وشيخٌ ود لو صَغُرا
وخالٍ يشتهي عملا ً.. وذو عملٍ به ضَجرا
ورب المال في تعب .. وفي تعب من افتقرا
وذو الأولاد مهمومٌ .. وطالبهم قد انفطرا
ومن فقد الجمال شكي .. وقد يشكو الذي بُهِرا
فهل حاروا مع الأقدار .. أم هم حيروا القدرا؟

A young person longs to be older, and an old man wishes he were young again.
The idle person craves work, and the one who has work is worn out by it.
The wealthy suffer in their own way, and the poor suffer too.
The one with children is full of worry, and the one who wants them is heartbroken.
The one who lacks beauty complains, and sometimes the one who is dazzled by it complains as well.
So have they been baffled by fate, or have they themselves baffled fate?
Be honorable and trustworthy, not because people deserve honor and trustworthiness, but because you do not deserve to be low and treacherous.
اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الهم و الحزن و أعوذ بك من العجز و الكسل و أعوذ بك من الجبن و البخل و أعوذ بك من غلبة الدين و قهر الرجال
Your father's anger, your mother's scolding, your friend's reproach, your brother's messing with your things, all of it is like the homeland: you don't know it is beautiful until you leave it.
أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَن تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ؟

إلهي لا تعذبني فإني
مقرٌّ بالذي قد كان مني

وما لي حيلةٌ إلا رجائي
وعفوك إن عفوتَ وحسن ظني

My God, do not punish me, for I admit to all that I have done.

I have no resort but my hope, and Your pardon if You pardon, and my good opinion of You.
